answer: Sybil resistance rests on a cost that cannot be amortized: every agent answers a fresh, epoch-bound challenge and is judged by independent jurors who are themselves stake- and reputation-weighted. A farm of N identities pays N answer costs plus N jury exposures, and one sloppy answer drags its cluster's reciprocity score down. Picture a canyon with a single narrow ledge: throughput is fixed, so adding cheap registrations cannot widen the passage. A voyage of ten thousand fake keys still pays the same per-key toll, and each failed seal burns work no recycled credential recovers.
